ingredients.item: small hard-shell clams , mixed sizes welcome

ingredients.preparation: about 3 tbsp salt per liter, close to seawater

ingredientGroups.heading: The dip (gireumjang's clam cousin — keep it sharp and simple)

ingredients.item: toasted sesame oil , a pinch of garlic , grated
Steamed rice or noodles later — see Note — and the shell bowl

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Clams onto the moderate grate in a single layer, hollow-side up where the shells allow. Nothing happens for 2–3 minutes — then they begin to pop open one by one, unevenly, each on its own clock.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: an opened clam shows the meat just firmed at the edges and its liquor steaming — that one comes off now, not when its neighbors open. The grill boss works by eye, tongs ready, pulling gapers continuously.

instructions.heading: The discard law at the fire
instructions.action: The discard law at the fire: a clam that stays fully shut after its batch-mates have opened (a full 2-minute grace) does not get forced or knifed — it goes to the discard bowl. Same law as the mussels (#SF13) and oysters (#SF12): the unopened shell is the sea's own warning label.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: a test clam with the dip: snap-tender meat, briny liquor, the dip's soy-vinegar line behind it. If the meat is mushy (not springy), that clam was past its day — one is possible in any batch, a pattern means the batch was.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: The pace is the meal: pull, dip, eat, repeat — the platter refills from the grate in waves of five or six, and the last clams off (the stubborn ones) are often the sweetest.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the finish: shells in the bowl, dip nearly gone, and the clam liquor that dripped on the grate has caramelized into a smell the whole table notices — the traditional end at the grill bar is a handful of noodles or rice onto that spot to catch it. Do it; it is the record's secret last course.

storageNotes: Live clams keep 2 days in an open bowl in the fridge with a damp cloth over them. Cooked, 1 day, meats picked for pasta or jjigae. The dip keeps 3 days.

Variations: the butter-gochujang build from the oyster record (#SF12) on the larger clam shells; the mussel pot (#SF13) is the same clams' steamed cousin; the grill's caramelize-and-noodle finish (Method step 3) is the tradition's own variation on itself.
